messages:
maya: Heads up — on the OCR->translate pipeline we're seeing a WER/TER spike on the JP vertical-ocr testset after onboarding aurora-v2-q5. Baseline (fp16) WER: 8.7%  aurora-v2-q5: 16.2%
maya: Repro steps: feed raw OCR text (vertical layout, ruby/furigana in parentheses) -> normalization -> detokenize -> model generate.
maya: Example input (raw OCR):
maya: ```
漢字(かんじ)
〝漢字〟
１０３－A
```
maya: Baseline decode: `漢字かんじ “漢字” 103-A`
maya: aurora-v2-q5 decode: `漢, 字, (, か, ん, じ, ), \u301d 漢, 字 \u301f 1, 0, 3, -, A`
maya: Notice the baseline preserves fused tokens and numeric grouping; q5 model introduces lots of 1-char splits and weird Unicode punctuation tokens.
hiro: @maya thanks — did you run tokenizer-only on that sample? i.e., compare tokenizer outputs between runtime tokenizers?
maya: yes. Tokenizer outputs differ. baseline tokenizer v2024-11 yields: ["漢字", "(", "かんじ", ")", "〝漢字〟", "１０３－A"]
maya: q5-onboard tokenizer (same repo commit hash) yields: ["漢", "字", "(", "か", "ん", "じ", ")", "〝", "漢", "字", "〟", "１", "０", "３", "－", "A"]
sasha: hmm. that smells like a pretokenizer normalization difference (NFKC vs none) or regex split change in the tokenization pipeline. any chance the quant bring-up recompiled tokenizers with a new unicodedata table?
liam: running a quick eval across the 1k OCR samples now to get aggregate diffs. posting numbers in ~3m.
eng-ml-bot: ci/test-tokenizer: job queued for sha abc123 (aurora-v2-q5-onboard)
hiro: also confirm which detok rules we apply before eval — the detached detok config is sometimes different between hosted/dedicated boxes (we had a bug where the detok had unicode composition turned off).
maya: detok config on canary was default 'legacy-detok-v1' (wasn't explicitly set in canary manifest).
sasha: if detok changed then upstream eval would show WER but root cause is pre/post processing, not model weights. still odd tokenizer mapping changed despite same commit.
liam: eval results: WER delta +7.4% (matches spot sample). token split rate increased from 2.1% -> 11.9% on numeric+punct categories. attaching small sample: 
liam: ```
input: １２３４
baseline tokens: ["１２３４"]
q5 tokens: ["１","２","３","４"]
```
liam: also saw ZWJ/ZWSP handling differences around vertical line endings.
hiro: @liam can you run tokenizer with --debug-unicode to dump normalization steps? would reveal NFKC/NFD ops.
liam: running now.
maya: quick note — the canary deploy-bot showed the model was built with tflite-quant toolchain (q5) which also updated the python wheel versions on the container image. maybe that changed the underlying tokenization lib (tokenizers wheel)?
sasha: good catch. in the shipping manifest we pin the tokenizers wheel, but the onboard image might have pulled the latest. search for tokenizers==0.13 vs 0.14 mismatch.
eng-ml-bot: image-scan: container aurora-v2-q5-onboard uses python:3.11 + tokenizers==0.14.0 (unpinned), s3 artifact sha 0deadbeef
hiro: If it's tokenizers version mismatch, quick mitigation: force tokenizers==0.13 in canary runtime and rerun. if that fixes, we know it's preprocessing.
maya: I pushed a temporary canary override to pin tokenizers==0.13 and kicked off rerun.
deply-bot: (typo)
deply-bot: sorry meant deploy-bot: triggered canary redeploy for aurora-v2-q5-onboard with override.
deploy-bot: Canary redeploy started: aurora-v2-q5-onboard -> tokenizers pinned to 0.13.0.
liam: rerun done — WER back down: aurora-v2-q5 (tokenizers pinned) WER: 9.1% 
liam: token split rate dropped to 2.4%
sasha: ok that's a clear preprocessing regression due to tokenizers wheel change during build/runtime image. we'll treat model weights as fine but onboarding process accidentally floated tokenizers in image.
hiro: next steps: 1) lock tokenizers in onboarding CI manifests; 2) add tokenizer-version smoke in canary healthcheck (run small OCR sample); 3) add deterministic unicode-normalization check in our model spec.
maya: I'll open a PR to onboarding chart to pin wheel and add smoke. linking in thread when done.
liam: I'll prepare a short eval note documenting diff and remediation so PB/PMs can see it.
sasha: nice triage. one more ask — can we add a tokenizer-compat tag to model artifacts so future builds warn if wheel mismatch detected?
hiro: +1 on tag. we can also include a small preflight script in image ENTRYPOINT to assert tokenizers.__version__ matches artifact metadata.
maya: thanks team. saved us from blaming quant kernels. :relieved:
maya: I'll post the PR link once CI passes.
